paragraph: Great questions deserve a careful hearing. Explore Christian debates, hear the objections and follow the reasoning wherever it needs to be examined.

blocks.text: Great questions deserve a careful hearing. Explore Christian debates, hear the objections and follow the reasoning wherever it needs to be examined.
Debates put convictions into conversation. Their real value comes when we slow down enough to distinguish a persuasive performance from a sound argument.
A debate asks someone to state a case, give reasons and explain how the conclusion follows.
Rebuttals reveal disputed premises, competing explanations and questions an opening speech can leave unanswered.
Use the exchange to identify a source to check, an idea to study or a question to carry into conversation.

Read supplied transcripts on this site, or follow the linked publisher where an on-site copy is not yet available. Each guide records known coverage limits. Use the recording to check the exchange in context.

Transcripts and recordings preserve the speakers’ arguments. Sources include participant organizations and independent transcript publishers; each page names its host and notes known coverage limits. These records are not Reformed teaching authorities. The connected guides state our scriptural and confessional position.
Listen with a pencil in hand.
Let the exchange become a study. These four habits help you follow both speakers fairly and decide what to examine next.
Write down the actual motion and define the key terms. Notice when either speaker moves to a different question.
List each speaker’s premises and conclusion. Try to restate the other person’s position in words they would recognise.
Find the premise or source on which the disagreement turns. Pause the recording and open the transcript or cited text.
Distinguish what was established from what still needs work. Record your question in the guide’s reflection box.
From the debate to a conversation.
A public exchange can sharpen a question. Patient, truthful conversation gives you a place to explore it with someone.
Conviction with an open Bible. Scripture first. Reformed convictions. Sources you can examine.
